feedback: If the chosen scale makes the largest value overflow the grid or produces awkward marks, prompt choosing a larger scale (e.g. moving from 2 to 5 or 10) so the biggest value fits.
If intervals are uneven, re-space them equally so each step up the axis adds the same amount.
Confirm ownership by having the learner read their own graph back through its scale and compare to the table.
activities.intendedInsight: Constructing a scaled graph requires choosing a workable scale from the data, keeping intervals equal and bars from the baseline, so that positions map back to the intended values.
learnerActions: Take a frequency table (e.g. swimming 20, cycling 15) and choose a sensible scale that fits the largest value with equal intervals (e.g. each square = 5, giving 4 squares and 3 squares).
Draw the bars from the baseline with equal width, each reaching the correct scaled position.
Alternatively draw a scaled pictogram with a stated key, using a part-symbol where the value is not a whole multiple of the key.
Check: does each drawn bar/row read back to the original data value when read through the chosen scale?
activities.title: Construct a scaled graph from a frequency table
